sasha: Heads-up — noticed a pretty sharp drop in prefix/priming cache hit rate (~32% relative) after the matmul-scheduler rebalance we rolled out this morning. p99 latency for small-chat flows +~18ms. Should we roll back the scheduler change?

anita: Yep saw it too. Running a diff of KV keys for identical prefixes — keys are different post-deploy even when tokens are identical. Repro fairly stable on canary.

mike: Quick paste of what I'm seeing (trimmed):
```
old_key: 7f3a1c9b2e4f
new_key: 7f3a1c9b3e5f  # single-byte difference in tail
prefix: "Welcome back!"
```
Looks like only tail bytes differ, not tokenization.

mike: I profiled the hot path — the matmul tiling/alignment change in PR #4523 shifted GPU buffer allocations so padding bytes at the end of the prefix embedding buffer are now uninitialized / have different data across runs. Our cache key is currently hashing the raw embedding buffer before zeroing tail padding.

ryan: ^100 — allocation / alignment changes can mutate the padding. Two options: 1) canonicalize key to only include logical token bytes (preferred), or 2) zero tail bytes before hashing. Option 1 is ideal but needs plumbing in a couple of hot paths. Option 2 is trivial and low-risk.

anita: Did quick sim: zeroing tail before hash costs ~0.15% throughput in microbenchmarks but recovers ~28% of the lost hit rate in end-to-end sims. Numbers: before rebalance hit=73%, after rebalance hit=41%, zero-tail patch -> 70%.

sasha: I don't want to rollback the scheduler if we can patch quickly. Can we get a hotfix that zeroes padding in the hash path, run it to canary, and then follow up with a more correct canonical-key approach?

mike: I'll open a PR for the zeroing hotfix now. Repro command I used:
```
# repro locally
python devtools/run_kv_repro.py --model=gpt-14x --prompt-file=tests/prefixs/priming.txt --trace
```
This generates the key diff output above.

mike: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4891 — small patch, unit + integration tests added for key determinism across alignment variants.

deploy-bot: Canary for "matmul-scheduler" paused in prod/us-east-1 (reason: prefix-cache hit regression).

ryan: Ran staging sim with PR-4891 applied:
```
staging scenario: 10k chat sessions
baseline (pre-rebalance): priming_hit=0.73, p99=95ms
post-rebalance: priming_hit=0.41, p99=113ms
post-patch (zero-tail): priming_hit=0.70, p99=99ms
```
Patch looks good — small perf delta but big hit recovery.

sasha: OK let's promote PR to canary after tests pass and monitor per-route hit & token-cost dashboards. If anything still anomalous, we'll revert scheduler.

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: canary apply PR-4891 -> matmul-scheduler canary. Monitoring alerts: priming_hit, p99, token-cost, kv_key_entropy.

anita: I'll keep an eye on the KV key fingerprints and open follow-up ticket to implement logical-key canonicalization (avoid raw-memory hashing).

mike: Thanks — will attach the repro traces and flame graphs to the ticket.
